Which graphics API the game uses. Takes effect the next time you launch the game, not live.

OpenGL ES (default): a native renderer written for this port. It is the default because it works on every device tested so far, including ones where Vulkan renders corrupted graphics. Start here; only change it if you have a reason to.

OpenGL ES + ANGLE: the same renderer, but routed through Google's ANGLE, which translates it to Vulkan, instead of your phone's own GLES driver. ANGLE is bundled inside this app, so it needs no minimum Android version and no system setting. Often faster once running, though a menu with many controls (Skirmish options) can stutter the first time it opens while ANGLE compiles what it needs; it does not stutter again until you leave and reopen that menu.

Vulkan: the original backend, through DXVK's Direct3D 8 to Vulkan translation. Faster than the others on phones whose driver handles it well, typically recent Snapdragon. But it depends entirely on that driver, and on some GPUs it produces magenta patches, distorted geometry or corrupted menus that no setting here can fix — PowerVR BXM and Samsung Xclipse have both been reported. If Vulkan looks wrong on your device, that is what the default is for.

The Custom Vulkan Driver and DXVK Config sections only appear when Vulkan is selected.

Custom Vulkan Driver (advanced, Adreno GPUs only)

Loads a Vulkan driver (a Mesa Turnip build) instead of your phone's built-in one, the same technique Winlator and AetherSX2 use. DXVK itself now only needs Vulkan 1.1, but some older Qualcomm Adreno stock drivers report even less (or have other bugs) — this Turnip build can let those phones run the game anyway. On a qualifying Adreno phone this is applied automatically — "Reset to Recommended" restores that automatic choice after you've imported something else.

This does NOT help Mali, PowerVR, or other non-Adreno GPUs — but those don't need it either: most Mali GPUs (Mali-G76, Mali-G57, and similar) already meet DXVK's Vulkan 1.1 requirement natively, no driver swap needed. This option is Adreno-only because Turnip only targets Adreno hardware, not because other GPUs are unsupported.

"Import Driver" lets you override the automatic choice with your own adrenotools-format driver .zip (for example from K11MCH1/AdrenoToolsDrivers or The412Banner/Banners-Turnip on GitHub). Takes effect next launch, not live.

Edits dxvk.conf directly, the same file the engine reads on startup — no rebuild needed, takes effect next launch. Useful settings if the game feels slow on your device:

d3d9.samplerAnisotropy = 2 (or 0 to disable) — lower than the default 16 to reduce GPU work on weaker hardware.
dxvk.hud = fps,drawcalls,submissions,pipelines — shows a small on-screen performance overlay.
dxvk.logLevel = none — keep this unless asked to change it; more verbose levels slow the game down.

One "key = value" per line. An invalid line is simply ignored by DXVK, so a typo won't break the game — worst case your change has no effect.

These turn on extra logging for bug reports — leave them all off for normal play, they can slow the game down or produce large logs. If someone reporting an issue asks you to turn one on, enable it, reproduce the problem, then use \"View Logs\" above to send the result.
Select a game folder first (above) to use these

Very detailed internal logging (UI, fonts, INI files) for chasing a specific hang or bug. Can grow to a huge log (50–100+ MB) over a long session — use \"Performance summary\" instead if you only need FPS numbers. (gx_trace.txt)

Draws the touch layer\'s own state over the game: current gesture, where your finger is, where the engine thinks the pointer is, and the camera scroll anchor. Turn this on to report control problems — a runaway map, a ghost building in the wrong place, an ability aiming somewhere you did not touch. (gx_touch_debug.txt)

Adds one short line per second showing where frame time goes (radar, audio, network, game logic, rendering). Safe to leave on for a whole play session — turn this on for FPS/slowdown reports. (gx_perf.txt)

Records what the sound system is doing: music and speech buffer levels, movie audio, and every source that starts or stops. Turn this on if you are asked for an audio log after reporting missing, stuttering or silent sound. (gx_audio_trace.txt)

Shows FPS, draw calls, submissions, and pipeline count directly on screen and in the log. Turn this on for GPU performance reports. (dxvk_hud.txt)

Checks every graphics call for correctness — catches real rendering bugs but slows the game down noticeably. Only turn this on when asked to reproduce a specific crash or glitch, not for everyday play. (dxvk_validation.txt)

Adds extra startup details about how the game talks to your GPU driver (exact display format and settings negotiated). Turn this on when asked to track down a rendering glitch specific to your device. (dxvk_verbose_log.txt)

1. "Select Game Folder" opens a folder browser on your phone's storage. Navigate to wherever you copied your own Command & Conquer Generals Zero Hour install (the folder containing INIZH.big, Data\, ZH_Generals\, etc.) and tap "Use This Folder".

2. If browsing looks empty, Android is asking for the "All files access" permission first — grant it in the screen that opens (this is a normal Android permission, no root involved).

3. "View Logs" shows the engine log and, if the game crashed, a native crash log — no computer or adb needed. Use the Share button there to send the log to yourself.

4. "Launch Game" starts the game with the folder you picked.
